mentions.author: delegate
mentions.story: Why you should never use Upwork
mentions.text:
I once interviewed for Upwork pro. They sent me an Xcode project and I had to make some changes to it.

However, the required changes referenced features and files which weren't in the project and made absolutely no sense.

Even worse, the project they sent me was the "Photomania" project from Stanford's CS193p class: [course]

But the copyright information (Copyright by Stanford University) has been ripped off from all the files and replaced with "Copyright (c) 2015 Upwork". No reference to stanford CS or anything like that, just copy and paste.

Which is very wrong in my book.

I wrote them a message and after some fruitless exchanges with 4 or 5 different support people, I've decided to…

mentions.author: xackpot
mentions.story: Ask HN: Becoming an iPhone app Dev.
mentions.text: I think the best place to start learning is going through the Stanford lectures notes at [course] and watching the videos at [link]. The strategy should be to finish one lecture in a day or two without rushing to the next lecture. Finish up the assignments and if you get stuck somewhere, search, learn, repeat. This way you would have learned quite a bit on specific topic and would be comfortable on the next topic. By lecture 10 you would be itching to write your own app, but don't succumb to the temptation and keep on finishing up the lectures. May be after lecture 18 you can explore things on your own. HTH

mentions.author: pohl
mentions.story: Model View Controller: History, theory and usage
mentions.text:
I was hoping this article would resolve something that I have been curious about. MVP (Model View Presenter) has been in vogue in the GWT world lately, as a result of Ray Ryan's seminal Google I/O presentation in 2009 and all of the open source projects spawned by it that attempt to reify the patterns therein (one of which is MVP).

[link]

As presented by Ray, the diagram of MVP shows that the view never speaks directly with the model object, and always uses the presenter as an intermediary.

I wonder, what is the difference between this idea and how MVC is practiced in the Cocoa universe? The present article talks about how it (Cocoa) uses the mediator pattern to accomplish the same…

mentions.text:
My theory as to why so many photo sharing apps:

(2007-2008 CS193P)
Stanford Apple iPhone app project involves twitter api -> many twitter clients created.

(2009-2010 CS193P)
Stanford Apple iPhone app project involves flickr api -> many photo sharing apps created.

[course]

"By this point, your Paparazzi app looks up real users on Flickr, finds and lists their photos and lets you view them up close by zooming and panning. It also plots these photos on a map and lets you browser photos by location."
